title: Show every text the lesson points to
statement: Put every text a learner must read in the lesson's main path, never only behind a control they must notice, and show any text the passage alludes to.
detail: In a Grade 3 reading build, one lesson carried a second, real published text paired with its story for weeks, but the player never read that field, so all of it was inert while the passage alluded to it. The rules that followed give the second text its own steps at the head of the reading phase, before the story, and keep the toggle between the two only as the way back, because a text reachable only from a control a child has to notice is one most children never read. An earlier fix that shipped the toggle alone was judged half the fix. The rules add that an allusion to nothing is worse than none, since it punishes the child who notices it.

evidence.quote: U1-L5 was authored with one for weeks and the v4 player never read the key, so all of it was inert — and the passage ALLUDES to it
An allusion to nothing is worse than no allusion: the child who does the work of noticing it is the one who gets punished for it.
The poem gets its OWN beats at the head of Phase B, before the story.
a second text reachable only from a control a child has to notice is a second text most children never read.
on its own it is half the fix.
